guards.rationale: Equal for every value the sim can hold: CombatState.turn starts at 1 and only increments (combat.py's turn counter), so `!= 1` and `== 1` partition identically. EXECUTED: the turn-2 hand still contains exactly one Luminesce (`luminesce count=1`), and it is there because cards/luminesce.py sets `retain = True`, not because the relic fired twice. Worth recording precisely because the retained card makes a second firing look plausible in the output.

guards.what: N2: `CardPileCmd.AddGeneratedCardsToCombat(list, PileType.Hand, Owner)` -- one BATCHED add of the whole list (RadiantPearl.cs:41) -- vs the sim's per-card add_to_hand loop (radiant_pearl.py:28-29)
guards.rationale: With CardsVar(1) the list has exactly one element, so batched and per-card are the same operation and no hook can observe an intermediate state. Recorded rather than skipped because the collapse WOULD matter at CardsVar(2)+ (a hand-size clamp or an on-add listener would see the cards one at a time), which is a constraint on any future ascension/upgrade of this relic. The overflow rule also matches: CardPileCmd.add_to_hand (cmds.py:500-512) sends the card to the discard pile once MAX_HAND_SIZE is reached.

The card is ported and matches the source: cards/luminesce.py is a 0-cost TOKEN Skill with exhausts=True, retain=True and `gain 2 Energy` (3 upgraded). This is a fresh generated card, not a CardModel.CreateClone, so PROMPT.md bug class 17 (shallow clones dropping per-instance state) does not apply -- checked deliberately, since three relics in the pool do hit it. NOTE per binding rule 7: cards/luminesce.py and Luminesce.cs are not hashed by this record.
